sections.label: National drug control policy criticism
sections.summary: Singapore's strict national drug control policy is necessary, effective and well-supported, but some critics helping inmates abuse the legal process have been criticised by the Courts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The reason for making this Statement now is this: we have a strict national drug control policy; it is necessary, it is effective and it is well-supported by Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But our approach has been criticised by some who are helping inmates to abuse the legal process.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Courts have said that they try and frustrate the legal process and prevent the penalties from being carried out.

sections.label: Misinformation and public support
sections.summary: The speaker will address attempts to spread misinformation and undermine drug policies, and show strong public support including for the death penalty.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Third, I will speak about some attempts to spread misinformation and try and undermine aspects of our drug policies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I will also show that, despite these attempts, there is strong public support for our approach and policies, including the death penalty.

sections.label: Dutch cocaine seizure 2023
sections.summary: Dutch Customs seized a record of over 60,000 kilogrammes of cocaine in 2023 alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In the Netherlands, a record of over 60,000 kilogrammes of cocaine was seized by Dutch Customs in 2023 alone.

sections.label: Amsterdam mayor narco-state warning
sections.summary: In January this year, Amsterdam Mayor Femke Halsema said the Netherlands risks becoming a narco-state.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In January this year, the Mayor of Amsterdam Femke Halsema said the Netherlands risks becoming a "narco-state".

sections.label: Fatal shootings and explosions
sections.summary: Since 2013 fatal shootings more than doubled, with 391 shootings, 90 explosions and 101 attempted explosive attacks in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Since 2013, the number of fatal shootings has more than doubled.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In 2022, there were 391 shootings, 90 explosions, 101 attempted attacks with explosives.

sections.label: Belgian cocaine seizure record
sections.summary: Last year Belgian customs seized a record amount of cocaine, more than customs and border officials in all of the United States.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Last year, the Belgian customs seized a record amount of cocaine more than the customs and border officials in all of the United States (US).

sections.label: Drug-linked killings since 2006
sections.summary: Since 2006, nearly 450,000 people have been killed, many believed linked to drugs and the drug trade.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Since 2006, nearly 450,000 people have been killed, a significant number of these killings are believed to be linked to drugs and the drug trade.

sections.label: 2014 drug possession law change
sections.summary: In 2014, it passed laws reducing drug possession from a serious offence to an administratively handled misdemeanour.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In 2014, it passed laws to reduce the offence of drug possession from a serious offence to a misdemeanour which is to be dealt with administratively.

sections.label: San Francisco overdose death rate
sections.summary: Last year, San Francisco's drug overdose death rate reached a record high, more than double the US national average.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Last year, San Francisco's death rate from drug overdoses reached a record high.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It was more than double the US national average.

sections.label: Oregon overdose deaths and re-criminalisation
sections.summary: From 2019 to 2022 overdose deaths more than doubled, and by 2024 Oregon re-criminalised possession of even small amounts of drugs.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: From 2019 to 2022, the number of drug overdose deaths more than doubled from about 600 to about 1,300.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: By August 2023, last year, a majority of people in Oregon wanted to repeal the measure and in 2024 this year, they reversed course.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: They re-criminalised possession of drugs for even small amounts.

sections.label: Malaysia cannabis seizures rise
sections.summary: In Malaysia, cannabis seizures jumped from 3,700 kilogrammes in 2021 to 6,200 kilogrammes in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If you look at Malaysia, cannabis seizures jumped from 3,700 kilogrammes in 2021 to 6,200 kilogrammes in 2022, just one worrying statistic – and there are many others.

sections.label: Singapore drug seizures and abusers
sections.summary: Last year CNB seized about $15 million worth of drugs, dismantled 25 syndicates, and abuser arrests rose 10%.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Last year, CNB seized about $15 million worth of drugs and dismantled 25 drug syndicates.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The number of drug abusers arrested increased by 10% from the previous year, while the number of cannabis abusers reached a 10-year high.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Health and Lifestyle survey conducted by the Institute of Mental Health in 2022 showed that the mean onset age of illicit drug consumption in Singapore is 15.9 years old.

sections.label: Drug rehabilitation recidivism rate decline
sections.summary: From 1993 to 2021, the two-year recidivism rate for those released from drug rehabilitation centre fell from 73% to 27.7%.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: From 1993 to 2021, our two-year recidivism rate for those released from drug rehabilitation centre (DRC) decreased by more than two and a half times, from 73% to 27.7%.

sections.label: Heroin trafficking capital punishment threshold
sections.summary: A person trafficking 15 grammes of pure heroin, enough to feed about 180 abusers for a week, faces capital punishment.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For example, a person who traffics 15 grammes of pure heroin, which is enough to feed the addiction of about 180 abusers for a week, will face capital punishment.

sections.label: Survey on death penalty deterrence
sections.summary: A study in areas where many drug traffickers come from found 87% believed the death penalty deters trafficking substantial drug amounts into Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, we did a statistically, scientifically valid study in the parts from which many of our drug traffickers come from.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It showed that 87% of those surveyed, this is nine out of 10, believed that the death penalty deters people from trafficking substantial amounts of drugs into Singapore; 83%, this is eight out of 10, believed that the death penalty is more effective than life imprisonment in deterring drug trafficking; and 86% believed that the death penalty deters serious crimes in Singapore.

sections.label: US fentanyl and global drug deaths
sections.summary: In the US, more Americans die from fentanyl abuse every 14 months than from all America's wars since World War II.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In the US, every 14 months, more Americans die from abusing fentanyl than from all of America's wars combined since the Second World War, from Korea to Afghanistan, every 14 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In 2021, the World Health Organization reported 600,000 deaths in 2019 which was attributable to drug abuse.

sections.label: View on removing death penalty
sections.summary: The speaker's view, based on evidence, is that removing the death penalty will significantly increase drug trafficking.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: My view, based on the evidence, you remove the death penalty, drug trafficking will go up significantly.

sections.label: CNB drug abuser arrests decline
sections.summary: In the 1990s, CNB arrested about 6,000 drug abusers per year, and now arrests about 3,000 per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In the 1990s, CNB arrested about 6,000 drug abusers per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: CNB now arrests about 3,000 drug abusers per year.

sections.label: Drug-related incest and fatal crash
sections.summary: A man was convicted of incest with his 17-year-old daughter after sharing meth, and a man on drugs crashed a rental car into a bus, killing himself and injuring seven passengers.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Early last year, a man was convicted of committing incest with his 17-year-old daughter after sharing methamphetamine (meth) with her.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In another case last year, a 31-year-old man: he had consumed various drugs, went on to drive under the influence of drugs, crashed his rental car into a public bus, killed himself; injured seven other passengers in the bus.

sections.label: Drug abuse harms foetus
sections.summary: A recent KK Women's and Children's Hospital literature review found that drug abuse by pregnant women can cause serious harms to the foetus.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: A recent literature review by the KK Women's and Children's Hospital, found that drug abuse by pregnant women can cause serious harms to the foetus.

sections.label: Parental drug offences and children
sections.summary: A 2020 Ministry of Social and Family Development study found children of parents who committed drug offences were five times more likely to come into contact with the criminal justice system.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: A 2020 study by the Ministry of Social and Family Development found that children whose parents had committed drug offences, were five times more likely than other children to unfortunately come into contact with the criminal justice system in the future.

sections.label: POFMA directions on capital sentence posts
sections.summary: In May 2023, POFMA directions were issued against 10 social media posts and two online articles containing false statements about a capital sentence meted out by the Courts.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For instance, in May 2023 last year, Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act, or POFMA, directions were issued against 10 social media posts and two online articles for containing false statements about a capital sentence meted out by the Courts.

sections.label: Uncarried-out PACP sentences
sections.summary: As a result of many such applications today, some PACPs' sentences have not been carried out despite their cases being decided more than a decade ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As a result of many such applications today, we have PACPs whose sentences have not been carried out, despite their cases being decided more than a decade ago.

sections.label: Post-appeal Applications in Capital Cases Act
sections.summary: To deal better with unmeritorious last-minute applications before capital punishment, this House passed the Post-appeal Applications in Capital Cases Act, which comes into force within a few weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And quite clearly, unmeritorious and an abuse of process.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, to deal better with this situation, to deal better with unmeritorious applications being filed at the very last minute before capital punishment is carried out, this House passed an Act, the Post-appeal Applications in Capital Cases Act, or PACC.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That Act will come into force very soon, within a few weeks.

sections.label: Court of Appeal dismissal
sections.summary: The application was dismissed by the Court of Appeal recently.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The application was dismissed by the Court of Appeal recently.

sections.label: Death penalty survey support
sections.summary: A 2021 MHA survey found 74% agreed or strongly agreed the death penalty should be used for the most serious crimes, including drug trafficking, and a 2023 survey showed 77%.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In a 2021 MHA survey, 74% of the respondents agreed or strongly agreed that the death penalty should be used for the most serious crimes, including drug trafficking.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We redid that survey last year, in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It now shows that 77% of the respondents agreed or strongly agreed.

sections.label: Support for drug-free approach
sections.summary: Almost 91% expressed support for Singapore's drug-free approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Almost 91% expressed support for Singapore’s drug-free approach.

sections.label: Preventive drug education programmes
sections.summary: SportSG has begun incorporating preventive drug education in its programmes and curricula for young athletes, IHLs will reinforce these messages, and a Drug Victims Remembrance Day will be introduced this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: SportSG has begun to incorporate preventive drug education in its programmes and curricula for our young athletes and to reinforce positive life values to remind our youths about pursuing excellence while keeping their minds and bodies healthy.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And in our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs), these messages will be reinforced at various junctures, such as orientation sessions and pre-departure briefings before students go on overseas trips.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And starting this year, we will introduce a “Drug Victims Remembrance Day”.

sections.label: Inaugural Drug Victims Remembrance event
sections.summary: An inaugural observance event will be held at Ngee Ann City Civic Plaza on 17 May this year, with a candlelight display to remember victims of drug abuse from Singapore and around the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: An inaugural observance event will be held at the Ngee Ann City Civic Plaza on 17 May this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We will be holding a candlelight display to remember the victims of drug abuse, not only from Singapore but from all around the world, because victims from around the world deserve our sympathy and thoughts.

sections.label: Roving exhibitions across Singapore
sections.summary: The event will be followed by roving exhibitions across eight different locations around Singapore from May to July.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The event will be followed by roving exhibitions across eight different locations around Singapore from May to July.

sections.label: CNB Drug Situation Report 2023
sections.summary: An MP asks the Minister what new initiatives the Ministry and CNB are considering after an 18% rise in new drug abusers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, with regard to the latest CNB Drug Situation Report 2023, which observes an 18% increase from 2022 of new drug abusers in Singapore, can I enquire from the Minister what new initiatives is the Ministry and, more specifically CNB, looking at to ensure that this number does not increase further?

sections.label: Five-year recidivism rate percentages
sections.summary: The MP asks whether the five-year recidivism rate follows the same percentages, 73% in 1993 to 27% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would the Minister also share if the five-year recidivism rate generally follows those same percentages – 73%, I believe, as recorded in 1993 to 27% in 2021?

sections.label: Amending Constitution for challenges
sections.summary: The speaker says that after a constitutional challenge last year, they may consider amending the Constitution so similar future challenges do not succeed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: What I was suggesting is that as we see how people file their applications, we learn.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And looking at the methodology, for example, if there is a constitutional challenge – and there was last year – we may have to consider whether we need to amend the Constitution to make sure that any future constitutional challenges of such a nature will not succeed.

sections.label: 18% increase in youth drug abuse
sections.summary: The passage states that Mr Singh asked about the 18% increase in youth drug abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Second, Mr Singh has asked about the 18% increase in youth drug abuse.

sections.label: Ethnic components of new psychoactive substances
sections.summary: The passage says there is no clear correlation, but slightly higher Chinese participation in new psychoactive substances compared with traditional drugs.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Are there ethnic components to new psychoactive substances?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I do not think there is a clear correlation, but we have seen a slightly higher level of Chinese participation, as it were, the number of Chinese who take these new psychoactive substances compared with the traditional drugs, if I can so refer to them.

sections.label: Embedding anti-drug message against positive spin
sections.summary: The passage asks how to embed the anti-drug message against multiple sides promoting a positive spin on drugs.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On the first question, how do we embed this anti-drug message in the face of an assault from multiple sides putting forward a positive spin on drugs?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think this goes to Mr Singh's question as well, because if you see what is happening, by decriminalising and making drugs available, people stand to make a lot of money, billions of dollars.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, there are listed companies around the world which want this and they finance non-governmental organisations (NGOs), they finance publicity, which sells the idea that soft drugs are good, they are harmless.

sections.label: Singapore as UN outlier
sections.summary: Singapore is described as an outlier in the United Nations and at international conferences.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And that goes, in a way, to the second question that Mr Pillai asked, Sir.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We are an outlier in the United Nations (UN), in international conferences.

sections.label: Young age of drug initiation
sections.summary: The average age at which children start taking drugs is relatively young, at 15.9 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The area that I have concern with, like some of the other Members, is that the age at which children start taking drugs is relatively young – an average of 15.9 years.
